hero.filename: Houses on Logan Circle and Rhode Island Avenue NW.jpg
hero.title: File:Houses on Logan Circle and Rhode Island Avenue NW.jpg
hero.source: Houses on Logan Circle and Rhode Island Avenue NW
hero.description: From right to left: 1205 and 1207 Rhode Island Avenue NW were built in 1878 for George W. Spears. 1209 and 1211 Rhode Island Avenue NW were built in 1878 for A.C. Jennings. 1213 and 1215 Rhode Island Avenue NW, built in 1887 and designed by architect George B. Phelps, were also built for Spears. The corner house, 18 Logan Circle NW, was also designed by Phelps and built at the same time for Spears. It is the previous home of author and journalist Ambrose Bierce. 17 Logan Circle NW was built sometime around 1878. All of the buildings are contributing properties to the Logan Circle Historic District and Greater Fourteenth Street Historic District.

gallery.description: The Iowa condominium is located at 1325 13th Street NW in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. gallery.title: File:12-15 Logan Circle NW.jpg
gallery.description: Houses located at 12-15 Logan Circle NW in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. They are contributing properties to the Logan Circle Historic District and Greater Fourteenth Street Historic District. 12 Logan Circle NW (far left) was built in 1885 and designed by Thomas Franklin Schneider. 13 Logan Circle NW (left) was built in 1881 and designed by James H. McGill. 14 Logan Circle NW (center) was built in 1903 and designed by Frederick B. Pyle. 15 Logan Circle NW (right) is the Old Korean Legation Museum. It was built in 1877 and designed by Thomas M. Plowman.

gallery.title: File:4-9 Logan Circle NW Washington, D.C.jpg
gallery.description: Houses located at 4-9 Logan Circle NW in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. They are contributing properties to the Logan Circle Historic District and Greater Fourteenth Street Historic District. From left to right: 4 Logan Circle was built around 1874. 5 Logan Circle was built in 1883 and designed by Emil S. Friedrich. 6 Logan Circle NW was built in 1878 and designed by Henry R. Searle. 7 Logan Circle NW was built in 1886 and designed by Robert Stead. 8 Logan Circle NW was built in 1885 and designed by Hornblower & Marshall. 9 Logan Circle NW was built in 1890 and designed by George P. Phelps.

gallery.description: Le Diplomate, a French restaurant, located at 1601 14th Street NW in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. gallery.title: File:1 and 2 Logan Circle - Washington, D.C (cropped).jpg
gallery.description: 1 and 2 Logan Circle is a Second Empire style building constructed in 1877 for Ulysses S. Grant Jr., the son of U.S. President Ulysses S. Grant.  It previously served as the Embassy of Venezuela and as a sanitarium.  The building now consists of eight condominium units.  It is a contributing property to the Logan Circle Historic District and Greater Fourteenth Street Historic District.

gallery.title: File:1441-1443 Q Street, NW.JPG
gallery.description:
Row houses, located at 1441–1443 Q Street, N.W., in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C.  Built in 1880, the Italianate-style homes are contributing properties to the Fourteenth Street Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994.


Previous occupants of 1441 Q Street, N.W., (right) include U.S. Representative Ernest Mark Pollard, attorney and Cosmos Club member David A. Chambers, writer David Chambers Mearns, and the National Motorcycle Retailers Association.  Previous occupants of 1443 Q Street, N.W., (left) include U.S. Representative Edwin William Keightley, physicians Mary L. Wooster and Walter Mallery Wooster, botanist Elmer Drew Merrill, botanist Frank Lamson-Scribner, chemist Henry Newlin Stokes, the Oriental Esoteric Society of Washington, D.C.'s Oriental Esoteric Center, and minister James Clarence Olden.

gallery.title: File:1303 - 1307 P Street, N.W..JPG
gallery.description:
Row houses and a six-unit condominium (right) located at 1303–1307 P Street, N.W., in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C.
Built in the 1870s, the Italianate-style homes are designated as contributing properties to the Greater Fourteenth Street Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994.

Previous occupants of 1303 P Street, N.W. (right) include William Hartzell, Matilda Coxe Stevenson and ethnologist James Stevenson, We'wha, Ezra B. Taylor, Bernhard Fernow, Joseph E. Washington, Public Printer of the U.S. Frank W. Palmer, and William Torrey Harris.

gallery.title: File:1530 - 1534 15th Street, N.W..JPG
gallery.description:
Row houses located at 1530–1534 15th Street, N.W., in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C.
The former residence of Alma Thomas is on the left-hand side.  It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) in 1987.  The former residence of Mary Jane Patterson is the center building.

Built in 1875 (left), 1880 (center), and 1892 (right), the Italianate and Queen Anne-style homes are designated as contributing properties to the Greater Fourteenth Street Historic District, listed on the NRHP in 1994.
